findings.evidence: `Conditional.lean:41-47` states `condIndep_of_indicator_condExp_eq` with `[IsFiniteMeasure μ]`; `mathlib/Mathlib/Probability/Independence/Conditional.lean:290-296` shows `condIndep_iff` also has `[IsFiniteMeasure μ]`, while the proof only uses finite-measure integrability/conditional-expectation lemmas.
findings.fix: Change the signature to `{μ : Measure Ω} [IsFiniteMeasure μ]` (or the equivalent `@Measure Ω mΩ`) and keep the same conclusion; probability normalization is not part of the claim.
findings.issue: `condExp_indicator_sup_eq_of_condIndep` assumes `[IsProbabilityMeasure μ]`, but the adjacent converse and Mathlib's `condIndep_iff` only require `[IsFiniteMeasure μ]`, so this loses the finite-measure generality used throughout the exchangeability API.

summary: The new projection theorem is stated too narrowly: it requires a probability measure where the surrounding conditional-independence API works for finite measures.
